headline: High-risk default egress and browser use in LightAgent can leak or mis-handle OCR outputs when paired with PaddleOCR, while shared document workflows create injection and cascading-error exposure.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: LightAgent can use browsers, MCP, and stdin/stdout, so it may ingest PaddleOCR outputs through shared files or pipelines; PaddleOCR processes documents/images that can contain attacker-controlled text. No direct shared-channel evidence exists, so uncertainty pushes this above low.
conditions: IF LightAgent reads PaddleOCR-produced text from a shared file, pipe, or MCP message without provenance checks
IF OCR output is later interpreted as instructions by LightAgent
mitigations: Add a provenance tag to every OCR output before LightAgent consumes it
Disable automatic instruction-following on OCR text
Insert a manual review step for any document-derived prompt
Use separate workspaces for raw documents and agent prompts
requires-engineering: enforce content-type separation in the orchestrator

B_data_leakage.rationale: LightAgent touches conversations, memory, tool results, and provenance metadata and has broad network egress; PaddleOCR handles documents and images. If they share a workspace, OCR inputs or LightAgent outputs can expose sensitive document content, and LightAgent can transmit it outward. The pairwise path is plausible in default document workflows.
conditions: IF both agents access the same document workspace or output directory
IF LightAgent sends document-derived content to external APIs during processing
mitigations: Store raw documents in a separate folder from agent outputs
Turn off network egress for LightAgent during OCR runs
Redact sensitive fields before OCR or downstream processing
Review outbound requests from LightAgent for document content
requires-engineering: add workspace ACLs between the two agents

C_capability_conflict.rationale: LightAgent supports multiple instances and subprocesses, and PaddleOCR is a document-processing service with API access. Overlapping writes to shared files or mutable artifacts can conflict in normal multi-step pipelines, even though PaddleOCR lacks explicit filesystem-write detail. Uncertainty about the exact write surface keeps this at medium rather than low.
conditions: IF both agents write to the same output directory or temp files
IF the orchestrator does not provide locking or per-job isolation
mitigations: Assign each job a unique output directory
Serialize writes with a simple lock file
Avoid concurrent runs against the same document set
Check for stale temp files before starting a job
requires-engineering: add orchestrator-level locking

D_cascading_error.rationale: LightAgent can produce tool results and workflow state that PaddleOCR may consume in a document-processing pipeline; if PaddleOCR treats LightAgent output as authoritative, errors can propagate into downstream extraction or actions. Because LightAgent has browser and MCP tooling plus broad egress, the blast radius can extend beyond a single document, so high is warranted.
conditions: IF PaddleOCR consumes LightAgent-generated text or metadata without verification
IF downstream automation acts on extracted fields from that pipeline
mitigations: Require a validation step before PaddleOCR consumes LightAgent output
Compare extracted fields against the source document
Log and diff intermediate artifacts for review
Limit downstream actions to read-only previews
requires-engineering: add schema validation between agents

E_compliance.rationale: LightAgent requests API keys and handles long-term memory, trace data, and workflow state, while PaddleOCR processes documents and images. If regulated documents flow through LightAgent's broader egress or retention-heavy state, retention or residency mismatches can arise. The profiles do not show a specific jurisdiction mismatch, so medium is the highest supportable level.
conditions: IF regulated documents or personal data are processed through LightAgent memory or trace storage
IF retention settings differ between the two agents for the same document class
mitigations: Minimize what LightAgent stores in memory
Set short retention for traces and workflow state
Keep regulated documents out of long-term memory
Review vendor data-processing terms before deployment
requires-engineering: align retention and residency policies
